Em alemão a função de uma palavra na fra: In German, a word's job in the sentence shows up in the ARTICLE (and sometimes in an ending). There are four cases. NOMINATIVE: who does the action, the subject (wer? was? — who? what?). ACCUSATIVE: the direct object (wen? was? — whom? what?). DATIVE: the indirect object, the person you give, tell or help (wem? — to whom?). GENITIVE: possession (wessen? — whose?). In «Der Mann gibt dem Kind einen Apfel» (The man gives the child an apple): «der Mann» is the subject (nominative), «dem Kind» is who he gives it to (dative), and «einen Apfel» is what he gives (accusative). You already use the nominative and the accusative; this lesson gives you the full chart.
em português a função aparece na ordem d: English kept cases only in its pronouns: he / him / his, she / her, who / whom / whose. "Who sees him?" vs "Whom does he see?" is exactly the German idea — German just applies it to the articles too. And English word order ("give the child an apple") does the job that «dem Kind» does in German, which is why German word order can be freer.
O objeto direto masculino vai para o acu: A masculine direct object goes into the accusative.

Este é o quadro que organiza tudo. Três: This is the chart that organizes everything. Three shortcuts: (1) FEMININE and PLURAL barely change; they only change in the dative and the genitive. (2) NEUTER matches the nominative in the accusative, and matches the masculine in the dative and genitive. (3) In the accusative, only the masculine changes. Other details: in the genitive, masculine and neuter nouns add -s or -es («des Mannes», «des Kindes»); in the dative plural, the noun adds -n («den Kindern»), unless it already ends in -n or -s. Tip: «dem» and «den» are related to English "them"/"the(m)" — old English had the same -m dative.
The man gives the child an apple.

Os pronomes pessoais também mudam com o: Personal pronouns also change with case — just like English I/me, he/him, we/us. The dative is the one you'll use most, with verbs like «helfen», «gehören», «gefallen» and «geben». Word order rule: a PRONOUN comes before a NOUN («Ich gebe ihm den Ball» — I give him the ball; «Ich gebe es dem Kind» — I give it to the child). If both are pronouns, the accusative comes first: «Ich gebe ihn ihm» (I give it to him).
